name: Use sample-and-hold as a processor on another modulator (not as a random source): step a sine LFO at a rate, automate the LFO rate and the S&H rate separately on a filtered-noise riser so the end seems to slow down through aliasing, and turn a regular step pattern into random hat-loop volume dips with the inverse amount on an FX mix, on a duplicated layer
goal: Delta beyond our random S&H LFO skill: here S&H samples an input modulator at its own rate. With a sine LFO (unipolar, full amount) into the S&H input, a low S&H rate gives coarse steps over the sine and a high rate follows it finely, so you keep the LFO's regularity with random-feeling steps. On white noise through a filter, map S&H → cutoff at a reduced amount; instead of a linear ramp LFO riser over four bars, put the LFO rate and the S&H rate on automation lanes, ramp the LFO rate to maximum and start the S&H rate low (individual steps audible), so near the end the sampled pattern sounds like it is slowing down. For hat loops, feed a random-drawn 4-bar step modulator (1/8 rather than 1/16) into the S&H and map S&H → volume (unipolar, ~80%) for random level dips, map the same S&H inversely to a metallic FX mix, and keep the processed loop as an extra layer over the original.

source.title: This is Sample & Hold | Cubase Modulators Explained
source.transcript_note: DAW modulator walkthrough; channel intro and comments CTA dropped.

prerequisites: DAW or synth where a sample-and-hold modulator can take another modulator as input, or Web Audio / JS: a step clock at rate r_sh that latches the current value of an LFO or step array and writes it with setValueAtTime to a gain or BiquadFilter frequency (implementation note)
White noise source with a filter
Hat loop, a volume/gain stage and an FX with a mix control (metallic/comb-like FX in the video)

inputs.name: sh_rate
inputs.description: S&H rate in Hz or tempo division (start low for audible steps)

inputs.name: lfo_rate
inputs.description: Input LFO rate; ramped to maximum in the riser

inputs.name: depth
inputs.description: Modulation amount (reduced on cutoff, ~80% on volume)

outputs.name: riser
outputs.description: Filtered-noise riser with stepped, decelerating-feeling motion

outputs.name: hat_variation_layer
outputs.description: Hat loop layer with random volume dips and inverse FX

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
An S&H with no input modulator does nothing; it must sample something.
Set the input modulator unipolar and to maximum amount so the S&H input spans 0–100%.
The slowdown at the end is a by-product (the fast LFO sampled at a lower S&H rate); it is not a tempo change.
A 1/16 step modulator was too fast for the hat variation; 1/8 worked. Values other than the ~80% volume depth and the 4-bar pattern were set by ear.

steps.action: Add a sine LFO and a sample-and-hold modulator, both in Hz. Route LFO → S&H input, LFO unipolar at maximum amount. Sweep the S&H rate from about 1 upward.
steps.expect: Large steps over the sine at low rates, fine steps at high rates

steps.action: Generate white noise through a filter and route S&H → cutoff; reduce the amount until it is not excessive.
steps.expect: Stepped random-ish filter movement on noise

steps.action: Compare with a simple riser: an upward-ramp LFO over 4 bars on both rates. Note it is linear and not editable; remove it.
Expose the LFO rate and S&H rate as automation lanes. Ramp the LFO rate up to maximum over the riser; start the S&H rate low and shape it with its own curve and a few random moves.
steps.expect: A riser with irregular steps that appears to slow down at the end

steps.action: For a hat loop: draw a random 4-bar step pattern on a step modulator at 1/8, route it to the S&H input (unipolar, max), and route S&H → loop volume (unipolar, ~80%).
steps.expect: Random level dips on otherwise steady hats

steps.action: Route the same S&H to the mix of a metallic FX with inverted amount, so the FX closes where the volume is high.
steps.expect: FX colour appears in the opposite places to the volume

steps.action: Duplicate the channel: keep the original loop and use the modulated version as a second layer; let other loops fill the quiet sections.
steps.expect: Added depth and variation without new samples

verification: With the S&H rate below the LFO rate, the modulation shows flat steps rather than a smooth sine.
In the riser, the last bars sound slower or irregular even though the LFO rate is at maximum.
On the hat layer, loud steps have less FX and quiet steps more FX.
The original and modulated hat layers play together without timing changes.
